subject: physics

hotspots.label: Sliding Book
hotspots.description: The object drawn across the strips — its sliding is what generates the friction we measure.
hotspots.colorHint: A plain hardcover book on the bench.
hotspots.function: Carries the sliding that friction resists.

hotspots.label: Surface Strips
hotspots.description: Three strips — sandpaper, wood, and ice — with very different friction felt by the sliding book.
hotspots.function: Provides surfaces of increasing smoothness to test.

hotspots.label: Friction Arrow
hotspots.description: The force arrow that points opposite the book's motion — that's the direction friction always acts.
hotspots.function: Draws the friction force pushing against motion.

hotspots.label: Force Gauge
hotspots.description: The reading in newtons showing how big the friction is for the current surface and press.

hotspots.label: Load Block
hotspots.description: An extra block you can drop on the book to press harder — and watch friction climb.
hotspots.function: Increases the normal force (press) to raise friction.

visualStyleNotes: Warm off-white paper backdrop, soft vignette, no floor grid. A long warm bench with three surface-strip tiles, a neat hardcover book, a coral friction arrow, and a pillar-mounted gauge. Neutral light, no bloom, no emissive. Saturated color only on arrow, gauge, strips
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0. Sandpaper tile: warm rough (roughness near 0.95). Wood: smooth mid (0.6). Ice: phantom glossy smooth (0.15, high clearcoat-like value). Book: amber cover smooth. Gauge: paper face.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: friction as the resisting contact force across varying surfaces and press.

GEOMETRY: a bench of length ~4.5 along +x with three surface tiles (sandpaper/wood/ice) at y=0.12 top, on wooden legs. Book (0.5×0.07×0.8) sits over the tiles, draggable along the bench. Gauge poles stand at the -x end; load block can stack on the book.

INTERACTION: surface selector moves the book across strips and the gauge recalcs force; load toggle adds the press block and friction rises accordingly.

NAMED NODES: BenchTop, SandpaperStrip, WoodStrip, IceStrip, Book, LoadBlock, FrictionArrow, GaugePlate. 6-10k tris.
